questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: You learn so much, when studying abroad, not just in a university, you also learn about life. You learn to live in another country, you learn a language, you learn to be independent because you are on your own, you learn to travel alone, and you learn to socialize.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study at Sorbonne because my main interest is French literature from the middle ages and the renaissance, and Sorbonne was just the right place for that. I also wanted to improve my French and follow courses in French, even though it could be difficult from time to time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think that it was not so easy because the French administration does not work well. For example we cannot choose courses online, we have to write them down in a paper and give it to the Erasmus-coordinator. We were told that we had to present ourselves to each teacher, so that they know we are Erasmus-students. The introduction days were a bit chaotic but when the semester began, I really started to enjoy it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We did get information about studying at Sorbonne and how to choose courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I recommend Cité internationale Universitiare de Paris, which was a very nice place to live. It was also close to Sorbonne.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's very nice living in the Cité, you have everything you need: a parc, a student restaurant where you can buy dinner for 3 euros, a nice bakery. You can also go to the theatre at the Cité, and there are many sport opportunities and events and concerts. It's a place where you won't feel alone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As I said, you have to write the courses you wish to follow with pen and paper. Then you will have to be a bit patient. I was not registered when the semester began and we had to wait for several weeks in order to be registered. Many students were complaining about it and I started to worry about it in the beginning as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The was an introduction day and that was it. We did not get much help, but maybe we did not need more help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful. I wanted to study French medieval and renaissance literature and French classicissm, so I chose my course from these periods. It was very interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient. It takes time to be registered, but it will happen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was very high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At the Sorbonne, it was mostly a teacher that spoke, and I only experienced group work a single time. I was satisfied because I just wanted to listen to the teacher's French and take notes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
La scène du Graal : entre poétique sérielle et pensée medievale
Naître, se marier, mourir à la Renaissance
La "poétique" du Printemps d'Agrippa d'Aubigné
Cultures féminines du Grand siècle
Le théatre de Samuel Chappuzeau
Victor Hugo, Odes et poésies diverses

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I may be one of the few students who enjoy ancient French literature. But if you love French literature, you are very lucky. Sorbonne has about 50 courses about French literature, so you can choose exactly what you like.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you take the train to visit another French city, then it is very expensive...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, it is not so expensive in France. In Denmark, it is more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were sometimes concerts at the Sorbonne and also many sport opportunities, but I did not try it myself because I had already much to do in Paris.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visit museums! It is free for students under 26, and there are so many museums in Paris.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the chateau de Versailles. Visit other cities in France with the train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I already felt part of the culture the first days.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to events, and there are many in Paris, and especially in the Cité Universitaire.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was not challenging, but in France, you have to say "monsieur" and "madame" to your teachers, also when you write an e-mail: "Chère Madame". And also say "vous" instead of "tu". Politeness is a part of French culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food. ;-)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You should strive to socialize and go to many events. It makes the experence abroad so much better.
You are here to learn and you should just enjoy it.
When you are in another city, you should also exlore it and not just study.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The French administration is horrible, and all students agree on that. Just be patient.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I have developed as a human being.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: One of the exam forms was especially challenging: when you have a 2-hour-exam where you write in French with a pen and paper.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
